days.title: West Coast Antiquities and Sights
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Gallarus Oratory
stops.detail: Outstanding among the sights is the Gallarus Oratory, a rustic corbelled building from early Christian times, which was built in dry stone technique like the Beehive huts of Fahan and the Killelton Oratory.

stops.name: Kilmalkedar
stops.detail: Another group are early Christian church ruins (Kilmalkedar and on one of the Magharee Islands).

days.title: Mountain Heights and Southern Shore
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Mount Brandon
stops.detail: Processions still take place here to Mount Brandon, the 952 m high third-highest mountain in Ireland, which can be seen from the Connor Pass like a row of ants in the distance.

stops.name: Inch
stops.detail: Of tourist interest are a very flat sandy beach at the spit of Inch and the Slea Head Drive, the western coastal road.

days.title: Eastern Forts and Southern Ruins
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Minard
stops.detail: Relics such as Cloghane church, the Garfinny Bridge and the pillar stones of Kilfountan and Reask, as well as the ruins of churches, monasteries, and old castles (Minard) belong to the landscape of the peninsula.

stops.name: Caherconree
stops.detail: The east, where the 600 m high fort Caherconree is located, is associated with Cú Rois and Cú Chulainn.
